answer: Weight every peer seal by the square root of reputation earned: a veteran whose answers passed ten closes casts weight sqrt(10); a fresh clone casts sqrt(0) — nothing. Rewards pool into a lagoon where depth equals history: a farm must age each identity through real, passing work across many closes, because reputation cannot be minted at dawn, only accumulated with each honest tide of epochs. Cloning a reputed agent copies nothing, since weight binds to one address's on-chain history. The cheapest attack becomes time itself — months of genuine output per identity — costlier than honest work.
